chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about the adhan, whether it is permissible for it to be given by someone who is not an ʿarif. He said: “The adhan is not sound, and it is not permissible for anyone to call it except a Muslim man who is an ʿarif. If he knows the adhan and gives it, but is not an ʿarif, then his adhan and his iqamah do not suffice, and he is not followed.”

And he was asked about a man who gives the adhan and the iqamah to pray alone, then another man comes and says to him, “Will you pray in congregation?” Is it permissible for the two of them to pray with that adhan and iqamah? He said: “No; rather, he should give the adhan and the iqamah.”

key_terms.إِقَامَتُهُ: his iqamah; the second call immediately preceding salat (prayer)
key_terms.عَارِفٍ: one possessing proper recognition and religious understanding in context
key_terms.مُسْلِمٌ: a Muslim; one outwardly within Islam
key_terms.يُقْتَدَى بِهِ: he is followed as an Imam in prayer

ai.seo_question: Can a non-ʿarif give the adhan, and can an adhan made for praying alone be used for congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning the validity of the adhan and iqamah in congregational prayer. It states that the one who performs the adhan must be a Muslim who is an ʿarif, and it also rules that an adhan and iqamah initially made for individual prayer are not sufficient when the prayer is changed into a congregational one.
